recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Do not add redundant prose or restore Composition.class wording; use Composition.category for the current element. Handle separate category value-set or DocumentReference mapping questions under their own trackers.
issue_request: FHIR-6918 was Published/Persuasive with Modification for DSTU1 and asked to clarify the relationship and usage rules between required Composition.type and optional Composition.class, or remove class if no rationale existed.
initial_application: No source commit explicitly mentioning FHIR-6918 was found. The duplicate FHIR-7104 links back to the original 6918 tracker. The closest application evidence is the same 2015 work referenced by the resolution: FHIR-5561 was applied in svn revision 5892 / git a4f7d63ab329bf6443e65c4ec50d5d88c53c029e as Composition.class and DocumentReference.class clarifications, and FHIR-8057 was applied in svn revision 5993 / git 995666d69f5f472f2f493a231edee9c2be1c967e as the Composition.class value-set update.
additional_context: Composition is active in source/fhir.ini. Later FHIR-17555 renamed Composition.class to Composition.category and increased cardinality to 0..*, and source/fhir.ini retains the migration alias Composition.class=Composition.category. FHIR-12652 later confirmed the old class element had become category and that the category binding is only an example binding. Zulip discussion in 2019 described the same coarse category versus fine type distinction, and Confluence refs found no FHIR-6918-specific contrary decision.
reconciliation: Published an empty audit commit. The authoritative current source already describes Composition.type as the required precise kind of composition and Composition.category as optional categorization for indexing/searching that may be implied by or derived from type.

related_jiras.note: Repeats the same type/class question and links to the original 6918 tracker, so it was not treated as an independent decision.
